To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiency of rectification is a function of frequency and dc load, that the efficiency of power management is a function of dc load, that power-management efficiency can be improved with reconfigurable networks, and that the power harvested by an array of rectifiers is a function of incident power density and the array size.
the harvested power and efficiency are improved with increasing array size, power density, and dc load; and that the efficiency is maximized at a dc load that is a fraction of the array power.
the power-management circuits can significantly increase the efficiency of RF energy-harvesting systems.

the design, analysis, and optimization of RF energy harvesting systems for low-power wireless sensor and communication networks.
the development of a novel energy-harvesting system that can be used for powering wireless sensor networks and other low-power electronics.
the design of efficient and scalable RF energy harvesters for wireless devices in a variety of environments, including the Internet of Things, wireless sensor networks, and wearable devices.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficiency of RF energy harvesting is limited by the efficiency of the rectifier, which in turn depends on the power density and frequency of the incident wave.

the power density of the RF source is a key parameter in designing the array and the rectification circuitry, and that a distributed array of antennas with a power management network is a promising solution for harvesting low-power densities in the 10-μW/cm 2 to 100-μW/ cm 2 range.
the power-management circuitry and the rectenna array are the two main factors that determine the overall efficiency of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with careful attention to power management, the efficiency of rectennas can be increased to 60-70% at high incident power densities and 20-30% at low incident power densities.
, for a given power density, the efficiency and harvested power increase linearly with the number of antennas in the array.
the power-management circuit must be designed for the specific array size, dc load, and frequency band.
